rules.description: Never challenge or throttle the sandbox control plane or the health checks — one region's sandboxes share an egress address, and a challenged health check pulls a healthy instance.
Requests for paths this product has never had. A scanner announcing itself.
A body far past anything any route accepts. The application's own limit produces a 413 with a request id; this is for the one whose only purpose is to be buffered.
Sign-up from something that does not look like a browser. A challenge, never a block: a bot score is a vendor's opinion and is wrong about somebody every day.
Signup velocity from one address — the first abuse signal the hosted platform has, and the cheapest to act on. Ten an hour is a household; fifty is a farm.
A ticket per socket, and a socket per reconnect. Loose enough that a deploy's reconnect storm passes, tight enough that a loop opening sockets does not.
The callback does a token exchange with a third party before it can decide the state is invalid, so an invalid one still costs a round trip somebody else has to serve.

The volumetric floor: whatever this deployment is asked for, at a rate no person produces. Deliberately looser than the application's own per-IP bucket, so an ordinary overshoot is refused by the layer that can say why.
No User-Agent at all. Recorded, never refused: curl, the test suites and every deployed agent calling an API send none, and the fallback debug client is somebody's browser.
